title: Runtime adaptive tuner: limiters, SLO routing, and anomaly rollback playbook
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem:
We want to aggressively recommend batching/caching configurations to reduce per-token cost, but automated changes must never violate latency/throughput SLOs. Past experiments showed transient tail-latency spikes when larger batch sizes or cache-promoting policies were applied during traffic shifts. We need an operator that can apply candidate tuning changes, monitor SLOs in real time, and automatically throttle/rollback when anomalies are detected.

Scope:
- Runtime components: limiter primitives (per-model and per-route), SLO-aware routing hooks, and an anomaly detector that consumes p50/p95/p99 + throughput and queue depth signals.
- Control-plane: safe-config apply API with staged rollout (canary -> ramp -> full) and automatic rollback triggers.
- Observability and playbook: dashboards, alert rules, and an on-call playbook for manual overrides.

Goals:
1) Never degrade confirmed SLOs (p95 latency and provisioned throughput) for production traffic.
2) Validate candidate batching/caching recommendations in a canary slice with synthetic traffic and automated acceptance checks.
3) Provide fast automatic rollback (< 90s median) when anomalies are detected.
4) Export decision traces for audit and postmortem.

Non-goals:
- Full autoscaling replacement (we integrate with existing autoscaler).
- Model architecture changes or kernel-level optimizations (handled by runtime team separately).
acceptance_criteria: Canary apply: candidate batching/caching config can be applied to a 1% traffic slice with zero manual steps.
SLO guardrails: if p95 increases by >15% relative to baseline or p99 increases by >5% absolute, the system automatically reverts to previous config within 120s.
Rate limiters: requests rejected due to safety limiters surface a clear error and are routed to fallback model variant or region per routing policy.
Anomaly detector: false positive rate <5% on historical test corpus, and detects injected regressions in synthetic test harness 95% of the time.
Observability: dashboard with per-candidate trace, commit ID, canary percentage, and rollback timestamp is available in Console and linked from apply job.
Playbook: on-call runbook covers manual rollback, failing canary investigation, and customer notification steps.
implementation_notes: Introduce a 'tuner-operator' microservice that receives config change requests and orchestrates staged rollout via runtime control-plane API.
Limiters design: token-rate limiter (tokens/sec), inflight-request limiter, and backlog-aware admission control. Limiters expose metrics and a binary pass/fail for acceptance checks.
SLO-aware routing: add dynamic routing rules that can divert a configurable fraction of traffic to fallback model variants when limiters hit thresholds.
Anomaly detection: ensemble detector combining EWMA of p95, robust z-score on p99, and queue-depth spike detection; detector runs on 10s windows for fast detection.
Safe apply flow: dry-run (simulate latencies on synthetic load) -> canary (1%) -> ramp (10% -> 50%) -> full. Each step requires health-check gates computed from real-time metrics.
Rollback mechanism: store previous config snapshot and execute immediate revert via control-plane API; emit UIs/notifications and tag commit with rollback reason.
Audit traces: persist each apply job with requestor, candidate diff, metric baselines, anomalies observed, and final outcome to the audit store.
decision_log: 2026-02-12: Chosen staged rollout model (canary -> ramp -> full) vs. instant apply due to prior regressions (decision by Marco Li, Aisha Khan, and Priya Desai).
2026-02-18: Ensemble anomaly detector selected over single-threshold approach to reduce false positives (decision by ML infra + Observability).
2026-02-22: Rollback SLAs set to 120s target with 90s median during tests (agreed with SRE team).
2026-02-27: Fallback routing will prefer regional fallback first, then downgraded model variant; customer-facing errors will include correlation-id.
testing_plan: Unit tests for limiter primitives and canary gating logic.
Integration tests with runtime: inject synthetic traffic profiles (steady, bursty, diurnal) to validate detector sensitivity and rollback timing.
Chaos test: randomly delay KV cache responses to ensure limiters and routing correctly divert and recover.
Load test: run nightly canary with production-replay for 2 hours; measure rollback latency and SLO impact.
QA signoff checklist: verify dashboards, alerts, and audit entries for 3 manually simulated failures.
